// src/string/words.ts
/**
* Regular expression pattern to split strings into words for various case conversions
*
* This pattern matches sequences of characters in a string, considering the following cases:
* - Sequences of two or more uppercase letters followed by an uppercase letter and lowercase letters or digits (for acronyms)
* - Sequences of one uppercase letter optionally followed by lowercase letters and digits
* - Single uppercase letters
* - Sequences of digits
* - Emojis and other Unicode characters
*
* The resulting match can be used to convert camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, and other mixed formats into
* a consistent format like snake case. It also supports emojis and other Unicode characters.
*
* @example
* const matches = 'camelCaseHTTPRequest🚀'.match(CASE_SPLIT_PATTERN);
* // matches: ['camel', 'Case', 'HTTP', 'Request', '🚀']
*/
const CASE_SPLIT_PATTERN = /\p{Lu}?\p{Ll}+|[0-9]+|\p{Lu}+(?!\p{Ll})|\p{Emoji_Presentation}|\p{Extended_Pictographic}|\p{L}+/gu;
/**
* Splits `string` into an array of its words, treating spaces and punctuation marks as separators.
*
* @param str The string to inspect.
* @param [pattern] The pattern to match words.
* @returns Returns the words of `string`.
*
* @example
* words('fred, barney, & pebbles');
* // => ['fred', 'barney', 'pebbles']
*
* words('camelCaseHTTPRequest🚀');
* // => ['camel', 'Case', 'HTTP', 'Request', '🚀']
*
* words('Lunedì 18 Set')
* // => ['Lunedì', '18', 'Set']
*/
function words(str) {
	return Array.from(str.match(CASE_SPLIT_PATTERN) ?? []);
}
export { CASE_SPLIT_PATTERN, words };


// src/array/groupBy.ts
/**
* Groups the elements of an array based on a provided key-generating function.
*
* This function takes an array and a function that generates a key from each element. It returns
* an object where the keys are the generated keys and the values are arrays of elements that share
* the same key.
*
* @template T - The type of elements in the array.
* @template K - The type of keys.
* @param arr - The array to group.
* @param getKeyFromItem - A function that generates a key from an element, its index, and the array.
* @returns An object where each key is associated with an array of elements that
* share that key.
*
* @example
* const array = [
*   { category: 'fruit', name: 'apple' },
*   { category: 'fruit', name: 'banana' },
*   { category: 'vegetable', name: 'carrot' }
* ];
* const result = groupBy(array, item => item.category);
* // result will be:
* // {
* //   fruit: [
* //     { category: 'fruit', name: 'apple' },
* //     { category: 'fruit', name: 'banana' }
* //   ],
* //   vegetable: [
* //     { category: 'vegetable', name: 'carrot' }
* //   ]
* // }
*
* @example
* // Using index parameter
* const items = ['a', 'b', 'c', 'd'];
* const result = groupBy(items, (item, index) => index % 2 === 0 ? 'even' : 'odd');
* // result will be: { even: ['a', 'c'], odd: ['b', 'd'] }
*/
function groupBy(arr, getKeyFromItem) {
	const result = {};
	for (let i = 0; i < arr.length; i++) {
		const item = arr[i];
		const key = getKeyFromItem(item, i, arr);
		if (!Object.hasOwn(result, key)) result[key] = [];
		result[key].push(item);
	}
	return result;
}
export { groupBy };

content.text:
The migrated file is at `out/module.ts`. It type-checks, and it bundles to 1606 bytes (min+gzip) with 110 bytes of your own code. I could not check equality against lodash or measure the original's size, because lodash is not installed here and I did not install it.

Three choices, all in `out/module.ts`:

- **`tokens` uses `es-toolkit/compat/words`.** The strict `words` splits `1st` into `1` and `st`. Lodash keeps `1st` as one word, and the compat version reproduces lodash's logic, so it is the one that matches the original within the input range.
- **`preview` uses `es-toolkit/compat/truncate`.** es-toolkit has no strict `truncate`, and this is the only library version that keeps lodash's `{ length }` call shape.
- **`byAge` uses strict `groupBy` with a one-line adapter, `(row) => String(row.age)`.** The adapter is needed because strict `groupBy` takes a function, not a property name. I did not use compat `groupBy` because it pulls in more code. The `String` wrapper gives the same string keys that lodash produces.

Checks I ran:

- **Type check:** `out/module.ts` has no errors. `tsc -p tsconfig.json` reports three errors in `src/module.ts` only, because `lodash/*` is not installed. That was already the case.
- **Size:** `npm run size -- out/module.ts` gives the numbers above. `npm run size -- src/module.ts` fails for the same missing-lodash reason, so there is no baseline to compare against.
- **Sample run:** I bundled the file and ran it on a few inputs. `tokens("ab1st")` gives `["ab","1st"]`, `preview` cuts at 21 characters plus `...`, and `byAge` groups by age as strings. These match what I expect from lodash, but I did not compare against lodash directly.

No other source files were created. The only other file I wrote is a scratch bundle and test script in the scratchpad.
